title: Board Book Navigation — UX Audit
method: Board UX audit (manual) · 5 lenses · Board personas (Margaret, David, Patricia, Robert) · grounded in Sauro's Big 4, Laws of UX, Shneiderman's 8 Golden Rules, Nielsen's 5 quality components
note: There is no board-specific ux-audit skill in this session; the FVDR ux-audit (Chris, Jim… and VDR data) does not apply to Board. This audit follows the same 5-lens structure with Board personas. Scores are expert judgement on the prototype plus the simulated task success from the usability study — not measured analytics. No Clarity or NPS data was available. Re-run 2026-10-22: Version 2 was replaced by the former Version 4 and re-scored; V1 / V3 scores are unchanged. Re-run 2026-10-23: Version 3 lost its reading-progress bar and was re-scored as built; both V2 and V3 now reflect their current state. Product decision 2026-10-23: agenda open by default and one phone tools sheet in every version — neither counts as a V2-only strength.
intent: Readers must (1) know which document and page they are on, (2) read a document continuously, (3) move to the next document — possible only through the viewer's navigation panels because continuous scroll stops at each document's end — and (4) jump to an agenda item's documents, annotate and search.

lenses.name: Intent alignment
lenses.question: Does the layout serve the reader's real job under the one-document-at-a-time constraint?

evidence.v1: Optimised for a PDF-editor mental model (top toolbar); the 'continue' action sits far from where reading ends.
evidence.v2: Same reading flow as V3 (one bottom pill for page / document), with zoom and annotation tools split into two more floating cards.
evidence.v3: Built around reading: document first, one bar for every reading action (page, document, zoom, annotations).

lenses.name: Findability
lenses.question: Can each persona find the next-document action, the agenda and the page jump without help?

evidence.v1: Agenda behind an unlabeled icon; ⌄ / ⌃ read as dropdown/collapse (Jakob's law — page turns are ‹ ›).
evidence.v2: Agenda open by default; ‹ › and |< >| in one predictable pill — but controls spread over three zones and all are icon-only.
evidence.v3: ‹ › |< >| and the page field in one predictable bar; agenda open by default (product decision). Icon-only controls.

lenses.name: Cognitive load
lenses.question: How many places must the reader scan, and how much must they remember?

evidence.v1: Two control zones (top toolbar + left card); icon-only tools.
evidence.v2: Three control zones on desktop (view card, palette, bottom pill) instead of four; one button on phones. Still more to scan than V3's single bar.
evidence.v3: One bottom bar + quiet top bar; Shneiderman 'reduce short-term memory load' is met best.

lenses.name: Interaction quality
lenses.question: Are controls reachable, consistent and giving feedback (desktop, iPad, phone)?

evidence.v1: Fitts's law: the next control is at the top while the pointer/eye is at the bottom; mobile tools in ⋯.
evidence.v2: Pill in the thumb zone; 'Fit' shown when fitted; pressed controls keep the hover fill. Tablet portrait still shows the two cards; pill buttons are 28px.
evidence.v3: Bottom bar in the thumb zone on iPad; consistent ‹ ›; no feedback that 'next' changes document.

lenses.name: Outcome quality
lenses.question: Do readers complete the tasks? (Sauro's Big 4: completion, time, errors, satisfaction — from the simulated study)

evidence.v1: Simulated success 77%, SEQ 4.5 / 7; Patricia fails US03 (thinks the pack ended).

v1.label: Not recommended
v1.text: Familiar for power users, but the top-only navigation fails low-proficiency and touch readers at document boundaries.

v2.label: Close second
v2.text: Same bottom-bar navigation as V3; with the agenda and the phone sheet now shared by every version, what remains is three control zones on desktop versus V3's one.

v3.label: Recommended — validate
v3.text: One control zone and a quiet top bar — the lowest cognitive load, with the agenda open by default and the shared phone sheet. Validate with R1 (labelled 'Next document') and R3 (local + global position).

risks: Document end stays silent — the bar must say 'Next document: <name>' on a document's last page (study R1). V2 and V3 have >| 'Next document: <name>' (tooltip only, icon button).
No variant shows how much is left since the progress bar was removed; global 'N / 7' without a local page count misleads about document length (study R3).
Icon-only controls exclude low-proficiency and touch users (study R4) — incl. V2's 6-dot phone trigger and V3's ⋯.
Agenda open by default and the shared phone sheet are product decisions (2026-10-23) not yet built into the V1 / V3 prototypes — implement before testing with real directors.
